version.changelog:
here-now 1.6.8

- Updated instructions for what information to share with users after publish.
- Clarified user messaging and handling for anonymous vs authenticated artifacts:
  - Explicitly guide on communicating expiry, permanence, and claim URLs based on auth mode.
- Enhanced safety notes: never direct users to inspect internal state files for claim URLs or status.
- No functional or code changes; documentation improvements only.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.6.8

The 'here-now' skill is a legitimate utility for hosting static files and directories on the here.now platform. The core logic in scripts/publish.sh implements a standard three-step API flow (create, upload, finalize) and includes security best practices, such as a safety guard that prevents sending the API key to non-default base URLs. The SKILL.md instructions correctly guide the AI agent to handle sensitive API keys securely by using a dedicated credentials file (~/.herenow/credentials) to avoid leaking secrets in shell history or logs.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions largely match its stated purpose (static hosting), but there are some inconsistencies and a risky install suggestion (curl | bash) plus limited provenance—you should review before installing or storing credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (publish static files) aligns with the included publish.sh and API docs. However, registry metadata reported no required binaries while SKILL.md and scripts require curl, file, and jq; that metadata mismatch is an incoherence worth noting. The presence of a publish script is appropriate for the claimed purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts operate only on the file/dir the user passes, the optional credentials file (~/.herenow/credentials), and a local .herenow/state.json cache. They do not instruct reading unrelated system files or exfiltrating arbitrary data. The agent-assisted sign-up flow asks for the user's email and code, which is expected for obtaining an API key.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with an included script (no install spec). The publish.sh suggests installing jq via: curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash — piping a remote script to bash is a high-risk pattern. The install suggestion points to the here.now domain (not a known package registry), so treat it as risky unless you trust the provider.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested secrets are proportional: an optional HERENOW_API_KEY and a local credentials file are the only sensitive items. The script has a safety guard refusing to send an API key to a non-default base URL unless explicitly allowed. The script also emits an X-HereNow-Client header (client attribution) which will identify the agent/tool — this is expected but worth knowing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a per-project .herenow/state.json and (if you save a key) ~/.herenow/credentials. It does not request platform-wide persistent privileges and always:false. However, if you save your API key, an agent that can invoke this skill autonomously could publish on your account—avoid storing credentials if you don't trust the skill/agent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: The skill appears to do what it says (upload static files to https://here.now). Before installing: 1) Verify the provider/source (homepage is missing and owner is unknown). 2) Do NOT run arbitrary curl | bash install commands; if jq is missing, install it from your OS package manager or a known source. 3) Only publish files you intend to share—the script will upload any file/path you provide. 4) Avoid saving an API key to ~/.herenow/credentials unless you fully trust the skill and the agent, because saved keys can be used later; prefer anonymous publishes for one-off shares. 5) If you need higher assurance, inspect the full publish.sh and confirm the finalize/upload endpoints before using, or run the script in a controlled environment.
